lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんが半濁点、つまり「゜」の付け方を教えて下さるそうよ
lines.en: Sho, your dad's going to teach you about handakuten — those little marks with the circle, the ones that soften the sound.
lines.style: Warm, almost conspiratorial tone. Gentle pacing. A small smile in the voice — she's delighted to share this news. Soft emphasis on 'handakuten' like she's letting him in on something special.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: メイ姉さん、ぼく、お父さんに片仮名のヽ、つまり繰り返し記号を教えて頂いたよ
lines.en: Mei-sis, Dad taught me about the repeat mark in katakana — that little symbol that saves you from writing the same thing twice.
lines.style: Quiet pride in his voice. Careful articulation — he's proud of learning something precise. Not boastful, just genuinely pleased. Slight brightness at 'Dad taught me,' like he's still glowing from it.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんが平仮名のゞ、つまり濁点繰り返しを書いて下さったわ
lines.en: Sho, your dad wrote out the voiced repeat mark for hiragana — the one with the dots that makes the voiced sound repeat.
lines.style: Gentle admiration in her tone. Speaking as if sharing something lovely she witnessed. Thoughtful pace. A warmth that says she's touched by his father's care.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: メイ姉さん、ぼく、お父さんと平仮名のゝ、つまり繰り返し記号を練習したよ
lines.en: Mei-sis, Dad and I practiced the hiragana repeat mark together — the plain one, without the voice marks.
lines.style: Eager but not scattered. A child's brightness mixed with focus. Clean articulation on the technical terms. Energy in 'practiced together' — he's excited about the shared time more than the mark itself.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんが片仮名のヾ、つまり濁点繰り返しを見せて下さったわ
lines.en: Sho, your dad showed you the voiced repeat mark in katakana — the one with the dakuten that makes it sound stronger.
lines.style: Soft, almost wistful. She's watching him learn through his father's patience. Measured pace. A gentle lilt that suggests she finds the whole thing rather touching.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: メイ姉さん、ぼく、お父さんに旧仮名のゐ、つまり古い「い」を教えて頂いたよ
lines.en: Mei-sis, Dad taught me about the old kana wi — it's not used anymore, but it's how they used to write the 'i' sound in classical Japanese.
lines.style: Careful, slightly awed tone. He's learning something that feels old and important. Deliberate pacing on the unfamiliar character. A hint of reverence — this is classical language, and he knows it matters.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんがゐる、つまり古文の「いる」を読んで下さったわ
lines.en: Sho, your dad read aloud the old form wiru — the classical way of saying 'to be' that you only find in old stories now.
lines.style: Dreamy, almost literary quality. Slower pace than before — she's savoring the sound of classical language. Like she's reading from something precious. Soft trailing-off at the end.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: メイ姉さん、ぼく、お父さんに爾、つまり古文の「それ」を教えて頂いたよ
lines.en: Mei-sis, Dad taught me the old character ni — it means 'that' in classical writing, the kind of words you see in ancient texts.
lines.style: Wonder mixed with earnestness. He's holding something fragile — old knowledge. Careful, almost reverent articulation. Slight pause before difficult kanji, like he's making sure he gets it right. Warmth when he says 'Dad taught me.'
